text:
Donald Trump is proposing new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the European Union, that would go into effect early next year, the office of the US trade representative said onWednesday.
The administration is proposing an additional 20% tax on Chinese imports, which would bring the total tax to around 40%. Other countries impacted by the new tariffs include Bangladesh, ‌Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.
In February, the supreme court ruled Trump’s so-called Liberation Day tariffs illegal. The court issued a narrow decision saying the administration had improperly used a specific emergency powers law to implement the tariffs, but did not broadly curb the president’s power to introduce new tariffs.
The administration is now using section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 as the legal basis for the new rounds of tariffs. The law gives the executive branch power to respond to unfair foreign trade practices after conducting formal investigations.
Though the White House did not give a timeline for the new tariffs, it said they could go into effect in January at the earliest. The US trade office said it would hold hearings on the new tariffs and its investigation into the unfair trade practices on 25 January.
This is the second major batch of section 301 tariffs, after the White House announced a broad slate of tariffs on more than 80 countries in July, including the UK, Mexico and Canada, saying the countries had failed to enforce bans on forced labor. A lawsuit fighting those tariffs is currently awaiting a decision in the court of international trade.
“For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favor while eroding America’s manufacturing base,” US trade representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement Wednesday.
“President Trump is proposing to take action to bring about the elimination of these unfair acts, policies, and practices. In doing so, we can level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.”
Tariffs have proven unpopular with US voters, who handed Democrats a decisive victory in the midterm elections that will give the party control of Congress. The Yale Budget Lab estimates that tariffs currently in effect have added an additional $900 in costs for each US household.
The rising cost of living was the number one issue for voters ahead of November’s midterm elections, according to a Harris poll survey for The Guardian. An earlier Harris poll found seven in 10 Americans blamed tariffs for higher prices.
Consumer prices rose an annualized 3.8% in October, the Bureau of Economic Analysis announced Wednesday, the highest rate since May and well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% annual target.
digest_he:
משרד נציג סחר ארצות הברית הודיע כי הנשיא דונלד טראמפ מציע להטיל מכסים חדשים על 14 שותפות סחר, בהן סין והאיחוד האירופי, אשר צפויים להיכנס לתוקף בתחילת השנה המיועדת. ההצעה כוללת תוספת מס של 20 אחוזים על יבוא מסין, מה שיעלה את סך המס לכ-40 אחוזים.

הצעד מגיע לאחר שבית המשפט העליון פסל בעבר מכסים קודמים שהוטלו באמצעות חוק חירום, ולכן הממשל מסתמך הפעם על סעיף 301 לחוק הסחר משנת 1974 המאפשר תגובה למדיניות סחר בלתי הוגנת. מדינות נוספות המושפעות מהמהלך כוללות את הודו, יפן, קוריאה הדרומית וטאיוואן.

המהלך צפוי לעורר דיונים ציבוריים רחבים סביב יוקר המחיה והשפעת המכסים על הצרכנים האמריקאים. לפי הערכות כלכליות, מדיניות זו כבר הביאה לעלויות נוספות ניכרות עבור משקי הבית בארצות הברית בתקופה האחרונה.
